newsitem.title: UK: World oil demand growth to accelerate in 1998 - IEA.
newsitem.headline: World oil demand growth to accelerate in 1998 - IEA.

text.p: Robust economic activity in developing countries and a return to consumption growth in the former Soviet Union will lift world oil demand next year, the International Energy Agency said on Friday.
World demand is expected to rise by 1.85 million barrels per day (bpd) to 75.5 million bpd, slightly surpassing 1997 growth of 1.75 million bpd, the IEA said in its monthly Oil Market Report.
But a 1.95 million bpd surge in production from suppliers outside the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) will be more than enough to satisfy the extra demand, it said.

"The world oil market in 1998 is expected to be well-supplied, as growth in non-OPEC oil production is anticipated to exceed the growth in world oil demand," said the IEA, which monitors oil market trends for members of the OECD.

The IEA revised lower its estimates of non-OPEC output in the fourth quarter of 1997 by 500,000 bpd and for the whole year by 100,000 bpd due to delayed new field starts and production problems, leaving more room for OPEC oil.

"The estimated call on OPEC crude has been raised by 200,000 bpd for 1997 as a result of downward supply revisions in the third and fourth quarter 1997 related to delays in North Sea fields and a more conservative view of production from existing fields in the UK sector."
